text:
Alex Chen: Heads up — ran into inconsistencies between our Python/Go/Rust SDKs when we try to switch exporter endpoints at runtime. local dev uses REDWOOD_OTEL_PROFILE=dev which points to local collector, but in Dedicated we flip endpoint via env var and some services keep sending to the old endpoint after SIGHUP. Anyone seen this?

Maria Gonzales: yep. Go SDK honors OTEL envvars and the collector switch, but the Rust wrapper keeps the OTLP exporter locked in because we create it at init and never rebind. Python is somewhere in between because the auto-instrumentation spawns background threads that cache exporter config.

Ben Patel: are we doing hot-reload for exporter endpoints intentionally? I thought the plan was: restart service for production to guarantee clean exporter lifecycle.

Alex Chen: we try to avoid restarts for Dedicated customers. They want endpoint failover (region fallback) without downtime. Need a safe hot-reconfig approach.

Sofia Iqbal: idea: standardize a small control API in each SDK that can be called to reconfigure exporter/processor. e.g. sdk.reconfigure_exporter({endpoint: "x"}) — libs implement graceful drain, swap exporter, continue. That avoids signals.

Ben Patel: sounds good. but tricky across languages: Python GC + thread pools, Go goroutines + channels, Rust ownership. We need a shared contract: drain timeout, fallback exporter, and config precedence rules (env var override vs explicit API).

Alex Chen: proposed contract: 1) config precedence: explicit API > app config file > env vars (still respected at cold start) 2) reconfigure API must trigger a drain of in-flight spans with a configurable timeout (default 2s) 3) SDK must be able to atomically swap processors/exporters and report status back (ok/failed)

Samir Rao: for retention/ingestion tagging we also need per-tenant resource attrs to be re-applied on swap. Suggest keeping a lightweight "profile" concept: REDWOOD_OTEL_PROFILE=staging|prod|dev which maps to endpoint, retention-days, and sampling policy. SDKs lookup profile map via embedded defaults but allow runtime override.

Maria Gonzales: agree. sample envvars i'm thinking:
```
REDWOOD_OTEL_PROFILE=prod
REDWOOD_OTEL_OTLP_ENDPOINT=https://otlp.redwood.internal:4318
REDWOOD_OTEL_RETENTION_DAYS=30
REDWOOD_OTEL_DRAIN_MS=2000
```

Alex Chen: also need to handle exporter handshake failures during swap — fallback to a noop exporter and surface metric + log, rather than blocking application. Infra wants telemetry eventually, not a hard dependency on exporter reachability.

Infra Bot: deploy-notice: added a canary to region-us-east for svc-encoder.otel-hot-reconfig=true

Ben Patel: lifecycle: implement reconfigure API in Go first (lowest friction), then mirror in Python (wrapper around opentelemetry-python SDK) and Rust (our internal otel-rs wrapper). We should add e2e tests that simulate collector endpoint switch and verify no spans lost beyond drain window.

Sofia Iqbal: testing checklist: unit for swap mutex + no deadlocks, integration with our collector (accepts both old/new endpoints), property test for per-tenant attrs preserved, and chaos test where exporter endpoint rejects handshake during swap.

Samir Rao: metrics: add exporter_swap_total (labels: service, result=ok|fail), exporter_drain_duration_ms, exporter_active_profile. We'll need these surfaced in Console and as alerts if swap fails repeatedly.

Maria Gonzales: minor language details: Python auto-instrumentation needs a global _OTEL_WRAPPER singleton to be replaceable. We'll document init order: call redwood_otel.init(...) before importing heavy libs. Go: use sync/atomic.Value for processor pointer swap. Rust: use ArcSwap or similar for atomic swap of Box<dyn Exporter>.

Alex Chen: docs + rollout plan: 1) design spec in docs repo 2) implement Go + unit tests 3) add Python shim + integration tests 4) Rust implementation 5) small canary across infra via feature flag 6) expose metrics & Console dashboard 7) wide rollout.

Ben Patel: one more: retention changes should be advisory to collector (header or resource attr) not baked into spans. we add resource.attr.redwood.retention_days so ingest can apply retention.

Sofia Iqbal: +1. also add a migration note: existing clients that rely purely on envvar changes will need to call sdk.reconfigure_exporter(...) or restart. We'll add a convenience script that does in-place reconfig via our agent endpoint.

Alex Chen: sweet. I'll spin up a spec doc and a small PR for the Go API. tagging @Sofia @Ben for tests.

Samir Rao: happy to pair on Prometheus + Console dashboard for swap failures.

Alex Chen: thanks all. I'll post the spec link when it's up. :thumbsup:
